sections.section_name: Section B (Short Answer Questions - 3 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Explain why copper is extensively used for electrical wiring whereas sulfur is not.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Copper is a highly ductile metal with abundant free electrons, making it an excellent conductor of electricity. Sulfur is a non-metal insulator that shatters easily.

questions.question_text: Describe the practical activity with aim: 'To test materials for malleability by hammering.'. Outline key steps and conclusion.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Steps: Place each sample on an anvil surface., Strike each sample firmly 3-4 times with a hammer., Observe whether sample flattens into a sheet or breaks into pieces.
Conclusion: Metals possess malleability (flatten under impact), while solid non-metals are brittle.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study - 5 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Provide a comprehensive comparison between metals and non-metals covering five physical properties and two chemical reactions.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Physical: 1. Lustre: Metals shiny, non-metals dull. 2. Hardness: Metals hard (except Na, K), non-metals soft/brittle. 3. Malleability: Metals flatten, non-metals break. 4. Ductility: Metals form wires, non-metals cannot. 5. Conductivity: Metals conduct heat/electricity, non-metals insulate. Chemical: 1. Metals + Oxygen -> Basic Oxides. 2. Non-metals + Oxygen -> Acidic Oxides.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: An artisan designing traditional musical instruments requires metallic wires that produce a resonant musical tone when plucked and can withstand high string tension.
Question: Which physical properties of metals make them suitable for musical strings?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sonority (ability to produce a sustained ringing musical sound) and high tensile strength/ductility (ability to be drawn into wires that stretch without snapping).

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study - 5 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Compare the reaction products when magnesium and sulfur burn in oxygen, and explain how litmus paper identifies their oxide nature.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Magnesium burns to form Magnesium Oxide (MgO), which dissolves in water to form Mg(OH)2, turning red litmus blue (Basic Oxide). Sulfur burns to form Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), forming sulfurous acid in water, turning blue litmus red (Acidic Oxide).
